claim: A two-layer ReLU MLP trained by gradient descent in the NTK regime converges, along any ray from the origin outside the training support, to a linear function of distance along that ray, at rate O(1/t).
stance_target: a specific, provable, positive mechanism for why gradient-ascent optimization against a neural-network surrogate's mean can admit unbounded off-distribution maximizers uncorrelated with the true (bounded/nonlinear) oracle function
scope_conditions: Two-layer ReLU MLPs trained with squared loss in the NTK regime (infinitely wide, appropriately initialized); empirically confirmed to hold approximately across varied depths, widths, learning rates, and batch sizes
quoted_support: "As t -> infinity, f(x0 + hv) - f(x0) -> beta_v * h for any h > 0, where beta_v is a constant linear coefficient... for t = O(1/epsilon), we have |f(x0+hv)-f(x0))/h - beta_v| < epsilon."

claim: ReLU MLPs extrapolate well only when the target function is itself approximately linear along the relevant directions from the training distribution; for most nonlinear target functions, ReLU MLPs do not extrapolate well regardless of architecture depth or width.
stance_target: identifying the condition under which a neural-network surrogate's off-support predictions would (or would not) track a nonlinear true oracle function
scope_conditions: Feedforward ReLU MLPs; contrasted with GNNs, which can extrapolate to algorithmic tasks when non-linearities are encoded in the architecture
quoted_support: "they can provably learn a linear target function when the training distribution is sufficiently 'diverse.' ... ReLU MLPs do not extrapolate most nonlinear functions."

claim: The paper's extrapolation results connect over-parameterized network training to the neural tangent kernel: optimization trajectories of over-parameterized networks trained by gradient descent are equivalent to kernel regression with a specific NTK, under the 'NTK regime' assumptions of Jacot et al. (2018).
stance_target: establishing the theoretical link between finite-network training and an exact kernel-regression equivalence, motivating why GP-like (kernel) machinery may behave differently in extrapolation than raw neural-network training
scope_conditions: Over-parameterized (wide) networks under the NTK-regime assumptions
quoted_support: "optimization trajectories of over-parameterized networks trained by GD are equivalent to those of kernel regression with a specific neural tangent kernel, under a set of assumptions called the 'NTK regime' (Jacot et al., 2018)"
